questions.stem: This illustration shows a supine patient secured to a table that is tilted head-down with the legs elevated. What is the primary hemodynamic purpose of placing a hypotensive patient in this position?

choices.label: B
choices.text: To promote venous return and central blood volume (Trendelenburg position)

choices.label: C
choices.text: To improve diaphragmatic excursion in respiratory failure

choices.label: E
choices.text: To decrease cardiac preload in pulmonary edema

explanation.summary: The head-down Trendelenburg position uses gravity to shift venous blood from the legs toward the thorax, transiently augmenting venous return, preload, and cardiac output as a temporizing maneuver in hypotension.
explanation.whyCorrect: The head-down Trendelenburg position uses gravity to shift venous blood from the legs toward the thorax, transiently augmenting venous return, preload, and cardiac output as a temporizing maneuver in hypotension.
